key_insight: Physics-informed losses can be invalid on coarse-grained turbulent data, but linear constraints that survive filtering can be enforced exactly with a cheap projection.
engineering_relevance: For turbulence surrogate models, enforcing only filter-consistent constraints can greatly improve stability and conservation without the cost or closure error of full PDE residual penalties.
method: Train a Fourier Neural Operator on coarse turbulent fields.
Apply a closed-form Fourier-space projection to enforce continuity and global momentum exactly.
Optionally fit a constant subgrid energy flux to close the global energy balance.
evidence_signal: On 2D isotropic turbulence, the projection reduced continuity error to 5.0e-7 and momentum error to 8.6e-11, and increased bounded 448-step rollouts from 0.18 to 0.87; on Kolmogorov flow, test-time optimization was about 3300x more expensive per trajectory.
watch_item: The main caution is that enforcing unclosed nonlinear constraints can bake in a false closure unless the missing subgrid terms are modeled or the constraint is truly filter-consistent.
paper_title: Only Linear Constraints Survive Coarse-Graining: Evaluating Physics-Constrained Neural Operators on Stochastically Forced Turbulence
